title: Sell Mineral Rights in Foxfield, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Foxfield, CO | Arapahoe County
metaDescription: Own severed minerals near Foxfield, Arapahoe County? We handle title confirmation and send a direct written offer, start to finish.
heroLead: Foxfield is a small Arapahoe County town, and here is exactly how the sale process works if you own minerals connected to land nearby.
intro: First, we confirm what you actually own. Send us your deed, or if you do not have one, enough information for us to search Arapahoe County records: your name, the seller's name from any inheritance, or a legal description if you have it.

Second, we check whether the interest has ever been leased or produced. Foxfield-area acreage sits toward the southern edge of DJ Basin activity, so this step often turns up no production history, which changes how we price it but does not disqualify it from an offer.

sections.heading: Title confirmation
paragraphs: We pull recorded deeds and, if applicable, leases from the Arapahoe County Clerk and Recorder to confirm your exact fractional interest. This usually takes a few business days once we have your legal description.

sections.heading: Pricing
paragraphs: Producing interests price off a decline curve applied to your trailing production. Unleased interests price against comparable regional lease and sale activity, which for this part of Arapahoe County runs more conservative than core Weld County acreage.

sections.heading: Offer and closing
paragraphs: Once we agree on a number, we prepare the assignment paperwork, you sign, and we record the transfer with the county. Most Foxfield-area closings take two to four weeks.

sections.heading: Why we ask for a legal description upfront
paragraphs: A street address alone is not enough to search county mineral records accurately, especially for older severed interests around small towns like Foxfield. A legal description, section, township, and range, or the original deed, lets us search Arapahoe County records precisely instead of guessing.

faqs.question: I don't have a deed. Can you still find my interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, we can search Arapahoe County records using your name or inheritance details to locate your ownership.

faqs.question: How long does the whole process take?
faqs.answer: Typically two to four weeks from confirming title to closing, assuming no complications turn up.

faqs.question: Is my interest worth anything if it's never been leased?
faqs.answer: It can be, priced conservatively against comparable regional activity rather than production.

faqs.question: I only have a street address, not a legal description. What now?
faqs.answer: Send what you have. We can often trace a legal description from a street address through Arapahoe County assessor and deed records.

faqs.question: Do you charge anything for the title search?
faqs.answer: No, we cover the cost of researching your title as part of evaluating whether to make an offer.
